paper.title_en: Radio synchrotron limits on WIMP annihilation in the Frontier fields cluster Abell 2744
paper.abstract_en: Galaxy clusters are massive dark-matter haloes permeated by μG-level magnetic fields, but their diffuse radio emission makes them astrophysically complex targets for indirect searches. We analyse Abell 2744 (Pandora’s Cluster, <math altimg="si82.svg"><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>0.308</mn></mrow></math>), a massive, dynamically disturbed Hubble Frontier Fields cluster, using the six homogeneous integrated radio-halo flux densities of Rajpurohit et al.[1] from 150 MHz to 3 GHz. The smooth dark-matter distribution is tied to the one-halo Subaru weak-lensing NFW fit of Medezinski et al.[2]; the reference limits assume no substructure boost. We compute synchrotron spectra for the <math altimg="si9.svg"><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><msup><mi>e</mi><mo>−</mo></msup></mrow></math>, <math altimg="si20.svg"><mrow><msup><mi>μ</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><msup><mi>μ</mi><mo>−</mo></msup></mrow></math>, <math altimg="si8.svg"><mrow><msup><mi>τ</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><msup><mi>τ</mi><mo>−</mo></msup></mrow></math>, and <math altimg="si7.svg"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>b</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></mrow></math> channels over <math altimg="si83.svg"><mrow><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>χ</mi></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math>–200 GeV. Dark-matter-only fits are used only as spectral-shape diagnostics: the <math altimg="si9.svg"><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><msup><mi>e</mi><mo>−</mo></msup></mrow></math> template remains a poor fit, and the curved cosmic-ray forms give lower raw χ<sup loc="post">2</sup> values than any dark-matter template. Upper limits are obtained with a coverage-calibrated flux-ceiling statistic that profiles an unrestricted non-negative astrophysical contribution in each frequency bin. For the reference magnetic model <math altimg="si1.svg"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>5</mn><mspace width="0.16em"/><mi>μ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">G</mi></mrow></math>, <math altimg="si2.svg"><mrow><msub><mi>η</mi><mi>B</mi></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow></math>, the smooth-halo 95 per cent limits range from <math altimg="si84.svg"><mrow><mn>5.15</mn><mo linebreak="goodbreak">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>25</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> to <math altimg="si85.svg"><mrow><mn>1.99</mn><mo linebreak="goodbreak">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>22</mn></mrow></msup><mspace width="0.16em"/><msup><mrow><mtext>cm</mtext></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup><mspace width="0.16em"/><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math>; the uncertainty envelope spans <math altimg="si3.svg"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>–10 μG and <math altimg="si4.svg"><mrow><msub><mi>η</mi><mi>B</mi></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>0.3</mn></mrow></math>–0.7. The magnetic field dominates the systematic budget, followed by the one-halo weak-lensing uncertainty. The resulting limits are weaker than the strongest current dwarf-spheroidal and cluster constraints for standard s-wave WIMPs, but they quantify the sensitivity of the Abell 2744 radio halo to annihilation-induced synchrotron emission under the adopted smooth-halo model.
